# ADR-0004: Case structure generated by code, veneer generated by a model

## Status

Accepted — 2026-08-29

## Context

A case has two layers that look like one:

- **Structure** — who the culprit is, who was in which room in which interval,
  which fact has which scope, and the chain that leads to the deduction.
- **Veneer** — names, personalities, the scene description, the text a player
  reads.

The structure is what the solver has to prove deducible (RN-002), what the
validator has to check (RN-001, RN-003, RN-004) and what evals have to
reproduce. The veneer is what makes the game enjoyable.

Three constraints bear on who generates the structure:

- **Reproducibility.** The project's convention is to run every eval five times,
  because temperature > 0 makes a single run inconclusive. If the case itself
  also varied between runs, nothing fixed would be left to measure: a prompt
  regression would be indistinguishable from a harder case.
- **Cost and latency.** Phase 1 targets a valid case in under 60 seconds. With
  model-generated cases, every case the solver rejects costs money and another
  call.
- **Testability.** RN-001 to RN-004 are structural invariants. If the structure
  comes from a model, testing them requires an API key in CI and tolerates a
  different answer on every run.

## Decision

The structure is assembled by a seeded deterministic generator in
`firenze.generation.generator`. The solver, in `firenze.generation.solver`, takes
`Case` (never `CaseWithSolution`) and holds a veto: a case that is not deducible
is discarded and regenerated from a derived seed.

The model runs **after** the solver approves, and only writes text: names,
personality, scene prose, dialogue. It cannot create, remove or reassign a fact,
a scope, a position in the timeline or the culprit.

Same seed and same generator version produce exactly the same case.
`Case.generator_version` travels with the data, because changing the generator
changes what a seed means.

## Consequences

+ The whole of phase 1 runs without an API key: no cost, no network, no
  flakiness.
+ RN-001 to RN-004 become property tests over dozens of seeds.
+ Evals get a fixed floor: the same case on every run, so the variation being
  measured belongs to the model rather than to the mystery.
+ The solver becomes a genuinely independent verifier — it does not see the
  solution, and the function signature guarantees that rather than the
  discipline of whoever writes the next function.
+ Generation costs ~0.2 ms per case against a 60 second target.
− Variety is bounded by the constraint space the code knows about. Cases will
  feel structurally similar until that space grows.
− The generator accumulates combinatorial complexity that a prompt would express
  in three sentences; every new kind of clue is code, not text.
− The veneer needs a guarded boundary: a model rewriting a description can
  contradict the structure without noticing. It will require post-veneer
  validation, fact by fact.

## Alternatives considered

- **The model generates the whole case as structured JSON; the solver rejects
  and regenerates.** This is literally what RN-002 describes, and it gives
  narrative variety from day one. Rejected on reproducibility: without a fixed
  case, a prompt eval measures two variables at once. It remains the natural
  path if structural monotony becomes the dominant problem — that would be a new
  ADR, not an adjustment.
- **Hybrid: the model proposes a theme, code turns it into constraints.**
  Combines both worlds, at the cost of a schema for the theme, a
  theme-to-constraints translator, and a fallback for when the theme does not
  fit. Too much complexity for a constraint space that is still small.
